edition.en: The complete oration, from the second edition (Boston: James Munroe and Company, 1838), as transcribed from a scan on English Wikisource; the title page is omitted and paragraphs split across pages are rejoined. A leftover line-break hyphen (“in-corruption”) is closed up and one misprint of the 1838 printing (“Marveil” for Marvell) is corrected.
edition.zh: 演讲全文，据英文维基文库依扫描本所录的第二版（波士顿：詹姆斯·芒罗公司，1838）；略去扉页，被分页切断的段落已重新接合。合上一处残留的换行连字符（in-corruption），并改正 1838 年印本的一处排印错误（Marvell 误作 Marveil）。

basis.en: Delivered in 1837 and printed in 1837 and 1838; Ralph Waldo Emerson died in 1882.
basis.zh: 1837 年演讲，1837 年与 1838 年印行；爱默生卒于 1882 年。

note.en: Emerson’s address to the Phi Beta Kappa Society at Harvard in 1837, on what a scholar is for: not a bookworm but “Man Thinking”. Its second part is the best short account here of how to use a library without being used by it: books are “the best of things, well used; abused, among the worst”, and their one purpose is to inspire. Notice the lamps: when our own light fails, we go to the lamps that were kindled by older light. The Chinese translates that second part.
note.zh: 爱默生 1837 年在哈佛对斐陶斐荣誉学会的演讲，讲学者为了什么：不是书虫，而是“思考着的人”。它的第二部分，是本架关于怎样使用图书馆、而不被图书馆所用的最好的短论：书“用得好，是最好的东西；用得不好，是最坏的东西之一”，它的唯一用处是激发。请留意那些灯：当我们自己的光熄灭时，就去寻那些由更早的光点燃的灯。中文译出这第二部分。

excerpt.orig: Books are the best of things, well used; abused, among the worst.
excerpt.en: Books are the best of things, well used; abused, among the worst.
excerpt.zh: 书用得好，是最好的东西；用得不好，是最坏的东西之一。
